projectlens.title: ProjectLens
projectlens.summary: Browser-local change assurance: compare a change pack with its schedule and record the board response.
projectlens.problem: Change packs and schedules drift apart before board meetings. ProjectLens loads both in the browser, surfaces the largest conflicts with source dates, and records the human decision and its conditions.
points: One-click Northstar demo runs on bundled synthetic fixtures — no install, no upload.
Pytest and Playwright suites run in CI and assert the demo's exact outcomes.
The README states boundaries explicitly, including what the tool does not prove.
projectlens.note: Everything on the demo page is synthetic fixture data committed to the repo.

ai-evaluator.title: Output Gate
ai-evaluator.summary: A deterministic regression gate for saved LLM outputs: required and banned phrases, in CI, the browser, or via MCP.
ai-evaluator.imageAlt: Output Gate regression check workbench screenshot
ai-evaluator.problem: Prompt and model changes quietly reintroduce known output failures. Output Gate replays saved outputs against a phrase policy and returns a pass or fail as a CI exit code — no model call, no API key.
points: Runs in the browser or as a composite GitHub Action with sticky PR comments.
Optional MCP server so Cursor/Claude can run the same phrase gate while drafting.
Scope is stated plainly — it does not check facts; a fluent fabrication that avoids the banned list still passes.
ai-evaluator.note: Repository and package name: ai-workflow-evaluator. The portfolio name is Output Gate.

quicksupply.title: QuickSupply
quicksupply.summary: A supply-cover workflow for requests, agencies, teacher offers, compliance, and live status — source stays private; the store shows a recorded demo.
quicksupply.problem: School cover coordination can become a spreadsheet-and-message chain. QuickSupply shapes the job around request intake, sequential agency assignment, teacher availability, compliance checks, and status updates.
points: Separates school, agency, and teacher workflows instead of flattening them into one admin view.
Uses live status updates so bookings can move without manual chasing.
Recorded agency demo only — the repository and live app are not public.
quicksupply.note: Private MVP. The muted video is a walkthrough of the agency workflow; no public repo or hosted demo.

lakehouse.title: Marketing ML Lakehouse
lakehouse.summary: A local analytics loop that moves raw marketing CSVs through DuckDB, model training, checks, and a dashboard.
lakehouse.problem: Many analytics demos stop at a notebook. This repo packages the full local loop: ingest raw marketing data, model it, check it, and expose it through a dashboard.
points: Two commands from clone to running pipeline, using CSV fixtures committed to the repo.
CI rebuilds the whole DuckDB lakehouse from the demo data and runs shape, tolerance and leakage checks.
The Pages demo states on the page that metrics come from committed fixtures, not a connected ad account.
lakehouse.note: Local demo pipeline and browser console — not a hosted SaaS product.

happening-core.title: Happening Open Core
happening-core.summary: Event schemas and a deterministic quality benchmark: provenance, freshness and coverage scored in one command.
happening-core.imageAlt: Happening Open Core benchmark CLI thumbnail
happening-core.problem: Event datasets rarely say how trustworthy they are. Happening Open Core scores a dataset for provenance, freshness and coverage against a reference list, deterministically.
points: One command against committed example data; no third-party runtime dependencies.
CI tests assert the exact benchmark numbers, including the README's example score.
The README lists what is deliberately not here: no live feed, no scraping selectors, no customer data.
happening-core.note: The private Happening product is parked; this public core is what a stranger can verify. Archived on GitHub Aug 2026 — kept as a completed study/demo sample.

sentence.title: Sentence Similarity Analysis
sentence.summary: A compact NLP notebook showing embeddings, cosine ranking, and the limits of similarity as a signal.
sentence.problem: Similarity search is useful, but similarity is not the same as truth. This notebook is a small, focused demo of embedding comparison and retrieval caveats.
points: Uses transformer embeddings to compare sentence meaning.
Ranks examples with cosine similarity.
CI tests the ranking logic with deterministic local vectors, and says so.
sentence.note: Study notebook: clone the repository. There is no GitHub Pages demo app. Archived on GitHub Aug 2026 — kept as a completed study/demo sample.

pyspark.title: PySpark Kafka Streaming
pyspark.summary: Compact PySpark and Kafka examples: DataFrames, JSON event production, and Structured Streaming.
pyspark.problem: Streaming examples are often too big to actually read. This repo keeps three small scripts that run, with a docker-compose Kafka round trip behind one make target.
points: examples/basic_dataframe.py runs with Java and PySpark alone.
make demo runs the Kafka producer and Structured Streaming consumer via Docker.
CI compiles the examples and executes the DataFrame demo via spark-submit.
pyspark.note: Technical examples: clone and run locally. There is no GitHub Pages demo app. Archived on GitHub Aug 2026 — kept as a completed study/demo sample.

hr.title: HR Performance Analytics
hr.summary: A Power BI dashboard package for headcount, sales performance, absence, and stakeholder-ready reporting.
hr.problem: Dashboard work is only useful when someone can inspect the handoff material. This package keeps screenshots, PBIX files, data, and commentary together.
points: Covers summary, sales, and absence views.
Includes PBIX files and a methodology PDF for inspection.
The sample CSV is synthetic and the README says the automated checks cover only its schema.
hr.note: Handoff package: open PBIX and PDFs in the repo. There is no live web demo.

paper-trading.title: Paper Trading Research Engine
paper-trading.summary: A completed personal study in reproducible walk-forward backtesting. Kept on the archive shelf so the method is inspectable; not pitched as a product.
paper-trading.imageAlt: Paper trading research engine benchmark console screenshot
paper-trading.problem: Backtest results are easy to cherry-pick and hard to reproduce. This engine bundles every report with its provenance, and deliberately publishes only synthetic fixture numbers.
points: Two-command local demo against a committed synthetic fixture — no API keys.
CI runs linting, multi-version tests, CodeQL and a security audit.
The benchmark table is labelled synthetic; real market results are not published without full provenance. Not financial advice.
paper-trading.note: Personal research archive. Synthetic fixtures only — not a product for others to run as a trading system, and not financial advice.

england.title: Can England Win It
england.summary: An interactive World Cup scenario simulator, archived after the event with an honest postmortem.
england.imageAlt: Can England Win It scenario simulator screenshot
england.problem: Tools built for a single event go stale after it. This app ran 10,000 seeded simulations per scenario, and was archived with a postmortem instead of being left to rot.
points: Seed-deterministic simulation with tests for bounds, monotonicity and uncertainty ranges.
Recorded walkthrough on the store preview — npm test runs in CI before every deploy.
POSTMORTEM.md explains why archiving was more honest than a stale countdown.
england.note: This is a scenario tool, not a forecast or betting product.
